textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE GOLGI APPARATUS (Golgi complex, Golgi-Apparat) — an ORGANELLE inside a eukaryotic cell, NOT a cell and NOT a bacterium — centred in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with lots of negative space around the structures so labels can attach later. Fill the whole square edge-to-edge on a neutral dark-charcoal cytosol background with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Match the exact house look of a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (not heavy black strokes), gentle soft shading, each structure its own distinct soft colour fill. STRUCTURE: a POLARISED STACK of SIX SEPARATE, FLATTENED, DISC-SHAPED MEMBRANE SACS (cisternae) lying roughly horizontally one above the other like a loose pile of slightly warped pita breads, seen in section at a slight angle. Every sac must be clearly SEPARATE from its neighbours with a visible gap of cytosol between them — they must NEVER merge into one continuous tube, snake, pipe or spiral. Each cisterna is drawn as two closely-spaced membrane lines enclosing a VERY NARROW pale-cream LUMEN — thin and flat across the middle — whose ENDS SWELL into distinctly DILATED, ROUNDED RIMS, with the peripheral edge PERFORATED by small round fenestrations and drawn out sideways into a few fine soft-lilac TUBULES. Do not draw the sacs as thick plump sausages or a pile of doughnuts; they are very thin flattened discs with fat edges. The stack is gently CURVED like a shallow bowl and is strongly POLARISED — this polarity is the whole point of the picture. Use a continuous CIS-TO-TRANS COLOUR GRADIENT so the polarity reads without labels: the BOTTOM face is the CIS FACE, drawn distinctly CONVEX (bulging downward, toward the nucleus), washed WARM AMBER-ORANGE, and beneath it hangs a lacy, perforated, net-like tubular CIS-GOLGI NETWORK in a slightly warmer amber; the MIDDLE MEDIAL cisternae are the flattest and most regular and shift through soft TERRACOTTA-CORAL; the TOP face is the TRANS FACE, drawn distinctly CONCAVE (cupped upward, toward the cell surface), washed muted VIOLET, more dilated and more irregular than the cis sacs, and it peels away into an elaborate, branching, heavily reticulated tubular TRANS-GOLGI NETWORK in dusty INDIGO-BLUE. Arriving from the lower-left corner, a partly-visible ribbon of ROUGH ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM in cool grey-blue, its OUTER surface studded with tiny dark ribosome dots, releases a few small MINT-GREEN COPII TRANSPORT VESICLES with a faint fuzzy coat; between the ER and the cis face sits a small irregular grape-like ERGIC cluster of fused sea-green vesicles and short tubules. A couple of small MUSTARD-YELLOW COPI vesicles bud from the dilated cisternal rims and sit in the gaps between cisternae. From the trans-Golgi network, three or four larger CLEAR-BLUE SECRETORY VESICLES bud off toward the upper right, each a round membrane sphere holding a few darker cargo granules, one caught just pinching free on a thin neck, and one small dark slate-blue vesicle carries a bristly polyhedral clathrin coat. A scatter of tiny FREE ribosome dots floats in the cytosol, clearly detached from every membrane. CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC RULES: the GOLGI CISTERNAE THEMSELVES MUST BE PERFECTLY SMOOTH — absolutely no ribosome dots, granules, beads, bumps or stipple ON any Golgi membrane; only the ER ribbon in the lower-left corner is studded, and the contrast between the studded ER and the smooth Golgi must be obvious. Do NOT draw internal cristae, folded shelves or partitions inside the sacs (that would be a mitochondrion). Do NOT draw a double membrane pierced by nuclear pores, a nucleolus or chromatin. Do NOT draw a plasma membrane closing around the Golgi as if it were a cell, and give it no DNA or nucleoid. Do NOT draw green thylakoid grana or a chloroplast envelope. Do NOT draw a symmetric featureless stack of identical pancakes — the cis and trans faces must look clearly different in curvature, colour, dilation and in the networks attached to them. Do NOT reverse the polarity: vesicles ARRIVE at the convex amber cis face and DEPART from the concave indigo trans face. Do NOT draw a cell wall, capsule, nucleoid, plasmids, flagella, pili, cilia, chloroplasts, a vacuole, or a whole bacterium. Exactly ONE Golgi stack in the picture; no duplicates. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks in the image.
